name: TX-25
label: Safe R

key_factors: No Democratic polling or fundraising data
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, Roger Williams' incumbency and roughly $1.1 million war chest, and prediction markets pricing Democrats near 4% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with no evidence of Democratic strength to justify moving closer.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or polling showing Sims within single digits would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Roger Williams seeks another term in a central Texas district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $1.4 million raised and more than $1 million on hand, while Democrat Dione Sims has no reported fundraising totals. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on district fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets give Williams about a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's partisan lean and incumbency advantage. The race is rated Safe Republican, with Williams favored by roughly fifteen points and only modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
